SUMMARY

Amphenol Corporation(APH+3.52%)reported record sales and adjusted earnings for the third quarter of 2026, driven by a 77% organic growth rate in the IT Datacom market and the integration of the CommScope acquisition. Management announced a 20% dividend increase and a new $4 billion stock repurchase program while reporting a record book-to-bill ratio of 1.19 to 1. The company stated that demand for artificial intelligence applications now represents approximately three-quarters of its IT Datacom business, which more than doubled in scale year over year. The operational strategy involved expanding the product portfolio across seven end markets through organic developments and the acquisition of four companies specialized in automotive and electronics components.

Operator:Hello and welcome to the Third Quarter 26 Earnings Conference Call for Amphenol Corporation. Following today's presentation, there will be a formal question and answer session. Until then, all lines will remain in a listen only mode. At the request of the company, today's call is being recorded. If anyone has any objections, you may disconnect at this time. I would now like to introduce today's conference host, Mr. Craig A. Lampo. Sir, you may begin.

Craig A. Lampo:Thank you very much. Good afternoon, everyone. This is Craig Lampo, Amphenol's CFO, and I am here together with Adam Norwitt, our Chairman and CEO. We would like to welcome you to our third quarter 26 conference call. Our third quarter 26 results were released this morning I will provide some financial commentary, and then Adam will give an overview of the business and current market trends. Then we will take your questions. As a reminder, during the call, we may refer to certain non GAAP financial measures and make certain forward looking statements. So please refer to the relevant disclosures in our press release for further information.

In addition, as a result of our recently announced 2-for-1 stock split effective on 09/03/2026, all share and per share data discussed on this earnings call will reflect the split. The company closed the third quarter of 26 with record sales of $10.2 billion and GAAP and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.79 and $0.80 respectively. Third quarter sales were up 65% in U. S. Dollars and in local currencies, and 37% organically compared to the third quarter of 25. Sequentially, sales were up 17% in U. S. Dollars and in local currencies and up 16% organically. Adam will comment further on trends by market in a few minutes.

Orders in the quarter were a record $12.17 billion up a strong 99% compared to the third quarter of 25 and up 13% sequentially. Resulting in another very strong book to bill ratio of 1.19 to 1. This impressive book to bill was driven by robust bookings in most of our end markets with positive book to bill in all but 1 of our end markets this quarter. GAAP and adjusted operating income were both approximately $3 billion in the quarter, and GAAP and adjusted operating margin were 29.5%, 29.7%, respectively. On an adjusted basis, operating margin increased by strong 22 basis points from the third from the prior year quarter and declined a modest 10 basis points sequentially.

The year over year increase in adjusted operating margin was primarily driven by robust operating leverage on the significantly higher sales volumes which more than offset the margin dilutive impact of recent acquisitions. On a sequential basis, the slight decrease in the adjusted operating margin was driven by a meaningfully larger benefit from tariff recoveries in the second quarter. Excluding these benefits, our adjusted operating margin improved by approximately 70 basis points, reflecting strong conversion on higher sales levels as well as continued progress on profitability improvement at recent acquisitions, and particularly, CommScope. I am very proud of the company's operating margin performance in the third quarter which reflects continued strong execution by our team.

Bringing down third quarter results by segment, compared to the third quarter of 25, sales in the Communications Solutions segment, were $6.6 billion and increased by 99% in U.S. Dollars and 51% organically. And segment operating margin was 33.1%. Sales in the Harsh Environment Solutions segment were $2 billion and increased by 35% in U. S. Dollars and 29% organically. And segment operating margin was 30.1%. Sales in the Interconnect and Sensor Systems segment were $1.6 billion increased by 17% in U.S. dollars and 11% organically. And segment operating margin was 20%. The company's GAAP effective tax rate for the third quarter was 27.4%, and the adjusted effective tax rate was 27%.

Which compared to 23.5%, 27% the third quarter of 25, respectively. As is our typical practice, our adjusted tax rate excludes the tax effect of acquisition related costs and the excess tax benefit from stock option compensation as well as other discrete tax items. GAAP diluted EPS was a record $0.79 in the third quarter, up 61% compared to the prior year period. And on an adjusted basis, diluted EPS was a record $0.80 and increased by 74% compared to $0.46 in the third quarter of 25. This was an outstanding result. Operating cash flow in the third quarter was $2.1 billion or 102% of net income and free cash flow was $1.6 billion or 80% of net income.

An excellent result considering the growth we have experienced. From a working capital standpoint, inventory days, day sales out outstanding and payable days were all within our normal ranges. During the quarter, the company repurchased 3 million shares of common stock at an average price of approximately $81 And when combined with our normal quarterly dividend, total capital returned to shareholders in the third quarter of 26 was approximately $553 million As noted in the earnings release, the Board of Directors approved an increase in the company's quarterly dividend by 20% to $0.15 per share effective for payments beginning in January 2027.

As also noted in the earnings release, the company's Board of Directors approved a new 3-year $4 billion stock repurchase plan which will become effective on January 1, 2027. The company expects to complete the remaining purchases under existing stock repurchase plan by December 31, 2026. Total debt at September 30 was $17.9 billion and net debt was $12.6 billion Total liquidity at the end of the third quarter was $8.3 billion which included cash and short term investments on hand of $5.3 billion plus availability under existing credit facilities. Third quarter 26 adjusted EBITDA was $3.4 billion and our net leverage ratio was 1.1x at the end of the quarter.

We are very pleased with the company's robust financial position. I will now turn the call over to Adam, who will provide some commentary on current market trends.

Richard Adam Norwitt:Well, thank you very much, Craig, and I would like to extend my welcome to everybody on the call here today. And I hope you are having an enjoyable fall so far. I have to tell you that here in Wallingford, Connecticut, it is a truly beautiful New England fall day. As Craig mentioned, I am going to highlight our third quarter achievements and include a few comments about the acquisitions that we announced today. I will also discuss our trends and progress across our served markets and I will make some comments on our outlook for the fourth quarter and the full year 2026. And of course, we will have time for questions thereafter.

With respect to the third quarter, I am just so proud of our team. They drove truly excellent performance once again in the third quarter. Our results were significantly stronger than expected, exceeding the high end of guidance in sales and adjusted diluted earnings per share. Our sales grew from prior year by 65% in U. S. Dollars and local currencies, reaching a new record $10.2 billion. On an organic basis, our sales increased by 37%. Driven by strong organic growth of more than 20% in 5 of our 7 end markets. And I will talk about each of those markets in a few moments.

The company booked a record $12.2 billion in order in the third quarter, representing a book to bill of 1.19 to 1 Orders essentially doubled from prior year and were up 13% sequentially. And as Craig commented, our book to bill was positive in nearly all of our end markets. We are also very pleased to have delivered robust adjusted operating margins of 29.7% in the quarter, an increase of 22 basis points from prior year. The strong profitability is a direct result of the outstanding execution of the Amphenol team around the world. Who continued to manage well in a challenging cost environment. Adjusted diluted EPS grew 74% from prior year, reaching a new record of $0.80 per share.

And we generated record operating and free cash flow in the quarter, $2.1 billion and $1.6 billion respectively. Another clear demonstration of the quality of the company's earnings. Finally, I am really pleased that our board of directors has approved a 20% increase in our quarterly dividend to $0.15 a share, as well as the new $4 billion, 3-year stock repurchase program. I just cannot emphasize enough my pride in and my gratitude to the Amphenol team around the world. Our results this quarter once again reaffirm the value of the drive discipline, and agility of our entrepreneurial organization. As we continue to perform well, amidst a very dynamic environment.

We are also very pleased that this quarter, we announced 4 acquisitions, 1 of which closed in the quarter and 3 of which we signed definitive agreements for and expect to close between now and the end of the first quarter. First, we closed on the acquisition of Empire Electronics at the beginning of September. With 2026 full year revenue expected to reach approximately $320 million Empire is the leading manufacturer of complex interconnect assemblies for the automotive market. With a particular focus on automotive lighting applications. The company is headquartered in Michigan, with approximately 4.8 thousand employees worldwide. This company is included in our interconnect and sensor systems segment.

We are also excited that we signed definitive agreements for the acquisition of Advanced PCB, DexScreen Limited, and Humanetics. First, Advanced PCB is a US based manufacturer of high technology printed circuit boards for the defense and industrial markets. Company is headquartered in Colorado and expects full year sales of approximately $270 million this year. Advanced PCB has approximately 800 employees across their 6 facilities in the US, and will be included in our harsh environment solutions segment post closing. Next, DexScreen is an Ireland-based provider of fiber optic connectivity products primarily for the fiber-to-the-home applications In the communications network market.

With approximately 100 employees, DexScreen is expected to generate full year 2026 sales of approximately $90 million and will be included in the communication solutions segment post closing. Finally, Humanetics is a leading provider of precision force sensors specialty fiber optic sensing products, and micromachining solutions for the commercial air defense and industrial markets. The company has approximately 350 employees and expects full year 26 sales of approximately $70 million. This company will be included in our interconnect and sensor systems segment post closing. I just have to say our team was very busy this quarter. But we remain confident that our acquisition program will continue to create great value for the company.

Our ability to identify and execute acquisitions, and then, very importantly, to successfully bring these new companies into Amphenol. Remains a core competitive advantage for the company. Now turning to our served markets, I just want to reiterate how proud we are of Amphenol's broad and balanced end market exposure. Our diverse exposure across the electronics industry enables us to continue to participate across all areas of the global electronics industry each of which represents significant future opportunities for expansion. We also remain committed to continuing to broaden our portfolio across markets geographies, customers, applications, and products. As we build on the company's momentum to further strengthen Amphenol's position long into the future.

So with that said, the defense market represented 8% of our sales in the quarter, sales grew from prior year by a strong 42% in U. S. Dollars and 30% organically. And this was driven by robust growth across virtually all segments of the defense market. Sequentially, our sales grew by 12%, which was largely in line with our expectations coming into the quarter. As we head into the fourth quarter, we expect a mid single digit increase in sales from these third quarter levels. And for the full year 2026, we anticipate sales to increase by more than 35% primarily driven by strong organic growth as well as the benefit of acquisitions.

We remain very encouraged by the company's leading position in the defense interconnect market. Where we offer the industry's widest range of high technology products to both traditional and new defense equipment manufacturers. Amidst the current dynamic geopolitical environment, countries around the world are increasing their investments into both current and next generation defense technologies. With our expanded product offering, as well as the significant capacity expansions we have made in recent years, we are positioned better than ever to capitalize upon this long term demand trend. The commercial air market represented 3% of our sales in the quarter, Sales increased by 23% from prior year and 22% organically.

As we benefited from increasing aircraft production volumes coupled with continued progress in expanding our content on next generation commercial aircraft. Sequentially, our sales grew by 9% from the second quarter, which was much better than our expectations coming into the quarter. Looking into the fourth quarter, we expect sales to remain at the strong third quarter levels. And for the full year 2026, we anticipate sales to increase by approximately 20%. I am truly proud of our team working in the commercial air market. With the ongoing growth and demand for next generation aircraft, our efforts to expand our product offering both organically and through our acquisition program continue to pay real dividends.

We look forward to further capitalizing on our expanded range of product solutions for the commercial air market long into the future. The industrial market represented 18% of our sales in the quarter, Our sales in this market grew by 60% in U. S. Dollars and 25% organically. As we saw continued strong demand across the diversified industrial market, and as we benefited from the addition of CommScope's building connectivity business. On an organic basis, virtually all of our industrial submarkets grew in the quarter. With all 3 geographies also showing strong growth. On a sequential basis, sales grew by 7% from the second quarter which was much better than our expectations.

As we look into the fourth quarter, we do expect sales to moderate somewhat from these robust third quarter levels. For the full year 2026, we now expect sales growth of more than 50%, reflecting both strong organic growth as well as the benefit of acquisitions. We are very excited by the company's strength across the many diversified segments of this important market. I remain confident in our strategy to expand our high technology interconnect, antenna, and sensor offerings both organically and through complementary acquisitions. This strategy has enabled Amphenol to capitalize on the many electronic revolutions that continue to occur across the diversified industrial market. Thereby creating further opportunities for our outstanding team.

The automotive market represented 10% of our sales in the quarter, and grew 13% in U.S. dollars and 9% organically. This was driven really by strength in electric vehicles as we once again drove growth in all regions. Sequentially, our sales grew by 12% from the second quarter which was much better than our expectations. Reflecting the ability of our team to quickly execute on a range of opportunities together with some impact from the addition of Empire in the quarter. For the fourth quarter, we do expect a slight sales moderation from these third quarter levels, And for the full year 2026, we anticipate that sales will increase in the 10% range from prior year.

I remain very proud of our team working in the global automotive market. With the acquisition now of Empire, we have broadened our portfolio once again in particular around value add interconnect products to this important market. While there are no doubt pockets of demand uncertainty across the automotive market, our team continues to be focused on driving new design wins with customers who are increasing the content of new electronics being integrated into their next generation vehicles. We look forward to benefiting from our strengthened position in the automotive market for many years to come.

The communications networks market represented 8% of our sales in the quarter, Sales grew from prior year by 25% in U.S. dollars driven by the addition of CommScope. On an organic basis, however, sales declined by 28% from prior year. Due in particular to moderations in demand from the broadband market as well as from other communication network operators. On a sequential basis, our sales declined by 13% which was in line with our expectations. Looking to the fourth quarter, we expect a further decline in sales from these third quarter levels on continued softness in spending, particularly in broadband.

For the full year 2026, we expect sales growth of more than 40% driven by the CommScope acquisition partially offset by some organic decline. With our expanded range of technology offerings, following the acquisitions of both CommScope and Andrew, there is no doubt that we are well positioned with both service provider and OEM customers across the communications networks market. Our deep and broad range of products, coupled with our global manufacturing footprint, have positioned us well to support customers around the world whenever they choose to expand their networks. The mobile devices market represented 5% of our sales in the quarter, and we were very pleased that our sales grew by a strong 31% in U. S.

Dollars and 29% organically This was really driven by growth in wearables, handsets, laptops, and accessories. Which more than offset some modest decline in sales related to tablets. Sequentially, our sales grew by 32% which was much better than our expectations coming into the quarter as we were able to react quickly to support incremental demand from a number of customers. Looking to the fourth quarter, we now expect our sales to increase by approximately 35% from these third quarter levels. And for the full year 2026, we anticipate robust sales growth of more than 30% compared to prior year. I am extremely proud of our team working in the always dynamic mobile devices market.

As their agility and reactivity has once again enabled us to outperform expectations in the quarter and to capitalize on the opportunity of increased demand from our customers. I am confident that with our leading array of antennas, interconnect products, and advanced mechanisms, including hinges, designed in across a broad range of next generation mobile devices. We are well positioned for the long term. The IT Datacom market represented 48% of our sales in the third quarter. Sales in this important market grew by a very strong 100% in U. S. Dollars and 77% organically.

This was driven by continued acceleration in demand for our products used in artificial intelligence applications together with continued strong demand in our base IT Datacom business. On a sequential basis, sales increased by 30% from the second quarter which was substantially better than our expectation for a mid teens increase. I would say that the vast majority of our sequential growth was related to AI, which now does represent approximately 3-quarters of our IT Datacom sales. As we look towards the fourth quarter, we expect sales to increase again in the mid single digits from these very strong third quarter levels.

For the full year 2026, we expect our sales to more than double compared to prior year, driven primarily by strong organic growth as well as the benefit of acquisitions, including CommScope. We are more encouraged than ever by the company's position in the global IT Datacom market. Our team has done an outstanding job of both securing future business on next generation systems with a broad array of customers but also on executing on these exciting programs. In addition, I just wanna note that the team at CommScope continues to make great progress. In further penetrating the IT Datacom market with their advanced optical interconnect solutions.

Accordingly, we now expect CommScope sales in the IT Datacom market to more than double for the full year 2026 and we expect that those sales should represent roughly half of their sales for the full year and that compares to around a third of their sales. Last year. The revolution in AI has created a unique opportunity for Amphenol. Given our leading high speed fiber optic and power interconnect solutions. All of these high technology products are critical components in our customers' next generation systems. This creates a continued long term growth opportunity for our company. Turning to our outlook.

Obviously assuming the continuation of current market conditions as well as constant exchange rates, for the fourth quarter, we expect sales in the range of $10.3 billion to $10.5 billion and adjusted diluted EPS in the range of $0.81 to $0.83 This would represent a year over year sales increase of 60% to 63% and an adjusted diluted EPS increase of 65% to 69% compared to prior year quarter. I would just note that this guidance does not reflect any acquisitions that have not yet closed, and therefore, does not include advanced PCB, DexScreen, or Humanetics.

Our fourth quarter guidance represents also an expectation for full year sales of $36.9 billion to $37.1 billion and full year adjusted diluted EPS of $2.82 to $2.84. This outlook represents a full year sales increase of approximately 60% and an adjusted EPS increase of approximately 70%. Very strong performance. I would also note that we have upgraded our outlook for CommScope, which is included in this full year guidance. We now expect CommScope to achieve $5.1 billion in sales, and to contribute $0.18 to our 2026 adjusted earnings per share.

I just cannot express enough how grateful I am to the entire CommScope team for their amazing work as part of the Amphenol family. there is no doubt that 2026 has been a very special year for Amphenol thus far. I remain confident in the ability of our outstanding management team to adapt to the many opportunities and challenges in the current environment and to thereby continue to grow our market position while driving sustainable and strong profitability through this year and into the long term. Finally, I would just like to take this opportunity to express my gratitude and thanks to our entire global team. For their truly outstanding efforts here in the third quarter.

You should know that they worked unbelievably hard to deliver this level of growth and profitability and I am grateful to each and every 1 of them around the world. With that, operator, we would be very happy to take any questions that there may be.

Operator:Thank you, mister Norwitt. The question and answer period will now begin. Please limit to 1 question per caller. To ask a question, please press * followed by 1 on your If you change your mind, please press *1 again. When preparing to ask your question, please ensure your device is unmuted We have a question from Luke Junk with Baird. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Luke Junk:Great. Thanks for taking the question. I wanted to start with CommScope. Adam, maybe if you could just give us some insight into the guidance raise this quarter and then bigger picture, I would be really interested in your thinking on the virtues of their business model and the current tight supply chain environment and maybe within that, if you could also just comment on the work you are doing to secure fiber supply and your flexibility in that respect. Thank you.

Richard Adam Norwitt:Yeah. Thanks very much, Luke. Well, again, I just wanna commend the team at CommScope. Obviously, when we announced the deal, we talked about this company, you know, at signing as a $3.6 billion company. And here we are now $1.5 billion more than that this year And I think when we closed, we said we thought it would be $4.1 billion. So $1 billion more than at the beginning of this year. And that is just a direct reflection. Of the team's ability to execute in the face of the demand opportunity that is there. And that demand opportunity for sure is very strong in the data center market.

AI and related They also see strength in their industrial market. And even if the communications network, as I mentioned, you know, we have seen a little bit softness in the demand there, think the CommScope team is executing extremely, extremely well. And when I say executing, I really mean not just, you know, doing the things in the factory to make it happen. But also facing up to whatever challenges they may see in the marketplace challenges around getting enough people in the right places, challenging around getting materials of all sorts including glass and other things.

Mean, there are lots of constraints that are there in the world, and I think the team has done a fabulous job to diversify their supply base, to secure supply of everything that they need, including glass, and to make sure that the company is positioned to support their customers not just here in the third quarter and the fourth quarter of 26, but for the long term. And as part of the Amphenol family, they have the wherewithal to do that.

Because rather than being in a company that was naturally constrained from a capital perspective and a scale but in particular, given the financial condition of their prior parent, I would tell you that CommScope is taking full advantage of being part of Amphenol. Investing in new technology development, developing a multiplicity of options for all the things that they need, across the board as a manufacturer And I think that long term positions them very, very well for the future.

Operator:Your next question comes from the line of Varun Govindaraj with Bernstein. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Varun Govindaraj:Good afternoon, Adam, Craig. Congratulations on the strong quarter, and thanks for the question. I had a question related to NVIDIA architectures. So as we shift from Oberon to Kyber theoretically in 2028, we lose the backplane and then move into that PCB midplane structure. How do you think about that from an all content standpoint? And have you been having any conversations around this? Would love to get any qualitative color if you can share it. I know it is still early.

Richard Adam Norwitt:Yeah. Well, Varun, first of all, let me welcome you to our call. And second of all, I think will learn in the years to come that I am. I do not discuss specific customers, and, you know, I am not gonna delve into specific customers specific architectures. What I will say is this. I mean, I personally meet with customers all the time. I was meeting with a lot of customers even just in the last few days. Who are involved in lots of future architectures and what we hear from all of our customers across the board. Who are designing these next generation architectures. For AI, for whatever you call it, AI or SI or accelerated compute.

You name however you want to call it. They need more interconnect period. And that more interconnect means more copper high speed interconnect. It means more optical interconnect. It means more power interconnect. And it is really our ability to bring to them the breadth of those opportunities. The breadth of those products, the depth and the new developments that we are offering, the cap capacity, the capability to scale with them, that regardless of what individual 1 program or another designs or does not design, we hear from all of our customers a continuity of the intensity of the interconnect architecture. That we can bring to them.

Operator:Next question comes from the line of Amit Daryanani with Evercore. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Amit Daryanani:Yep. Thanks a lot, and good afternoon, everyone. Adam, if I think about the IT Datacom segment growing 30% sequentially, I think it is 2x, which you had initially expected. And I think you said most of this came from AI on the prepared comments. Just wondering, the upside and strength that you are seeing over yours, is that coming from customers essentially increasing their demand to you? Or was it more driven by your ability to fulfill existing demand faster than you had expected? And maybe you could just connect that upside to the fact that you are guiding December quarter up mid single digits for IT Datacom broadly. Is that again the underlying deployment cadence?

Is that more a function of what you think you could deliver? Thank you.

Richard Adam Norwitt:Well, thanks so much, Amit. Look. A 30% sequential demand on a market this size is an enormous, enormous achievement for our team. So I wanna say that first and foremost. I think also, you know, there is traditionally a little bit of seasonality that comes in certain markets. You know, hard to say what the seasonality of AI will be. We are still guiding to a growth in the fourth quarter from these very high levels. I think it is very substantial. You know? I do not think that it is gated to say that it is gated by demand or our abilities. I mean, we have been executing really, really well. For our customers on their demand.

And I think you know, strength in the third quarter it was not that anything was pulled in. It was just we satisfied our customer demand, and we were able to execute upon it. And right now, what we see in the fourth quarter is this kind of mid-single-digit increase. From already very, very high levels. So I do not think there is any sign of anything there except that, you know, the fact that they are still procuring at these high levels and that we are able to meet the moment of the demand from the customers is a really positive thing from my perspective.

Operator:Your next question comes from the line of Mark Delaney with Goldman Sachs. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Mark Delaney:Good afternoon. Thank you very much for taking my question. Congratulations on the strong results. I want to talk about EBIT margins, if you could please. Overall, non GAAP EBIT margins are nearly 30%, and that is actually the incremental conversion margin the company has historically targeted. I am sure you would like to drive profitability higher going forward, but maybe talk a little bit about the ability for the company to take up its year around incremental margins north of the historical 30% target, especially in light of some of the input cost dynamics that are at work in the industry? Thanks.

Craig A. Lampo:Yes. Thanks for the question, Mark. Yes. No, listen, first off, You commented on the 29.7% operating margins we had in the quarter, and certainly, we are extremely proud of achieving kind of those high levels of operating margins that we certainly think, you know, is deserved given the technology, you know, and the value we are bringing to, you know, to our customers. and that is not just in IT Datacom but honestly, in all of our markets. But you know, that is being driven by a few things.

You know, number 1, obviously, we have, significant technology, which I just mentioned and the value being added to our customers, I think, is just driving kind of those margins higher. We are able to share some of those margins with our customers. But you cannot do that, you know, without, you know, strong execution, strong cost discipline. You know, by our general managers. And they have just done an outstanding job of, you know, leveraging kinda the obviously, the volumes that they have. And these are really complex products that are really hard to make, but do it in a in a way that ultimately is able to drive margin for the business.

You know, we talked about this 30% conversion margin. You know, we increased this, you know, a little over a year ago now, and, you clearly, we have already started to kind of approach, you know, those levels. So I do not think we would really change our per se long term target yet. I am not saying that will not happen kind of in the future here. But there is no doubt, I think, as we continue to grow, you know, certainly organically and, you know, certainly, you know, the acquisitions will have some. Those.

They are gonna have some compression on margins as we go forward because typically those are not at the levels of profitability that the company is at. But certainly, our organic growth as we go forward, I would expect to continue to you know, increase our margins, you know, to some degree. And I certainly do not think this 29.7% is kinda the bottom in terms of where we are today. I think that, ultimately, as we grow as our revenue continues to grow, we should be able to expand those margins. So we will talk about longer term targets in terms of conversion. From there, but I get.

You know, essentially, you know, we would certainly expect to continue to be able expand those margins.

Operator:Next question comes from the line of Shreyas Patel with Wolfe Research. Your line is open. Please go ahead.

Shreyas Patel:Hey. Thanks so much for taking my question, and congratulations on the strong quarter. Maybe wanted to maybe hone in on the power portion of the datacom business. We know the broad trends that are driving up a rack power needs. Towards 800-volt architectures with higher bandwidth and lower latency. Demands. But curious how sizable power is now relative to your overall AI business and how fast are you seeing that transition to higher voltage designs?

Richard Adam Norwitt:Yeah. Well, thank you very much, and I would like to also extend my welcome to you for the first time, on our call. Look, we have talked for a long time about this sort of triumvirate of technologies in data center for us, high speed, optics, and power. And how those are all very, very important to the data center, to the people who are constructing these data centers, are architecting them, also very important to Amphenol. They each represent real pillar technologies inside our company, and we continue to double down on those pillar technologies.

And if you drill down into power, you know, we have been involved in power interconnect for, you know, nearly the entire modern history Amphenol going all the way back to our defense business high-voltage industrial business. So we have been working with extremely high power interconnect. Knowing how you package that interconnect for efficiency and safety, which are really the 2 greatest considerations that you have in a power connector. Know, at the end of the day, and I think I have said this before, like, these data centers are basically trying to do a simple thing, which is turn electrons into tokens.

And if we can help our customers use less of those electrons through the efficiency of the power interconnect while keeping everything safe and secure which you need to do especially as you reach to these very high voltage and power levels. Know, that creates an enormous amount of value for our customer. In terms of the scale of our power business, and we have a very significant offering in power I would tell you that, you know, across our AI business, you know, without giving, know, specific decimal level numbers, I mean, it is a very meaningful portion of what we sell.

Even if I would say high speed and optics is a little bit--is certainly more in that order. But we have a very, very strong leadership position in ensuring that our customers get the right power into their data center. We see this as a high growth opportunity as the chips. As the chip architectures consume more power and as our customers drive into new power into new power formats like 800 volt and beyond.
